groups.problem: Passing the original guests array to sendAddGuestsEmails misclassifies existing attendees as newly added guests.
groups.rationale: Both describe the same mixed existing/new attendee request and the same incorrect notification. Passing uniqueGuests resolves both.

groups.problem: Guest addresses are compared case-sensitively against lowercased blacklist entries, allowing mixed-case bypasses.
groups.rationale: Both identify the same unnormalized guest value in the blacklist comparison and propose consistent lowercasing.

groups.problem: Duplicate new addresses within one submitted guests array survive filtering and create duplicate attendees and invitations.
groups.rationale: Both report missing server-side deduplication within a single request, because the filter compares only against existing attendees.

problems: Mixed-case guest addresses bypass lowercased blacklist entries.
Plus-address aliases bypass the blacklist because guest addresses are not reduced to their base address.
uncoveredProblems: Plus-address aliases bypass the blacklist because guest addresses are not reduced to their base address.

problems: Duplicate addresses within one request create duplicate attendees.
Concurrent requests can each pass the existing-attendee check and insert the same guest.
uncoveredProblems: Concurrent requests can insert duplicate attendees because the existing-attendee check and insertion lack atomic uniqueness enforcement.
